I1.quote: Hydrogen adsorption experiments were conducted using a BSD-VVS&DVS gravimetric vapor adsorption analyzer. Samples were degassed at 200°C for 3 hours, followed by measuring the hydrogen adsorption isotherms at 77K over a pressure range of 0-50 bar.

I2.quote: This study presents a novel method for synthesizing hollow porous carbon spheres ... The resulting materials, CS850-4.5 and CS800-4, achieved high gravimetric H2 uptake of 4.5 wt% (77 K, 50 bar)

I3.quote: The resulting materials, CS850-4.5 and CS800-4, achieved high gravimetric H2 uptake of 4.5 wt% (77 K, 50 bar) and volumetric H2 uptake of 25.9 g/L (77 K, 30 bar), respectively.

notes: Five-page conference paper (ICAE2024, Energy Proceedings Vol 51) with its own methods and data; not an abstract without data, so not_primary does not apply. No retraction statement; is_retracted false; no statement that the H2 data were published before. Carbon majority: XPS (p. 3, Section 3.2) says 'the primary elements in the materials are carbon and oxygen', surface O 14.60-20.47 wt%; N and O doped, small residual Fe (p. 3). Surface area: BET from N2 isotherms (Section 2.2), measured on the same samples CS800-4 and CS850-4.5 whose H2 uptake is measured. H2 data: Fig. 4(a) total and excess gravimetric isotherms at 77 K to 30 bar (left axis wt%, right axis cm3/g STP);Table 2 gives wt% at 1 and 30 bar. For extraction: CS850-4.5 1-bar uptake is 1.9 wt% in Table 2 but 2.3 wt% in the text (p. 4); BET 2142 m2/g in Table 1 but 2140 m2/g in Conclusions (p. 5); 4.5 wt% at 50 bar is stated in text only (figure ends at 30 bar). Fig. 4(b) MOF-5, Max3 and AC-1 curves are taken from ref. 8, not measured here.
